:::{#def-little-o}
#### Little-o notation (dominates)

Let $f$ and $g$ be functions from the positive integers to $[0, \infty)$ with $g(n) > 0$ for every $n$.
We write $f(n) = o(g(n))$
if, for every constant $\eps > 0$,
there is an integer $n_0$ such that

$$f(n) \le \eps \, g(n) \quad \text{for every } n \ge n_0.$$

That is, $f$ is eventually smaller than any fixed fraction of $g$,
which is the strict counterpart of @def-big-o.
In this case we also say that $g(n)$ **dominates** $f(n)$.

:::
